title: Canonical finite coefficient comparisons in purity coordinates
statement: In the setting of [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts], define the pullback coefficient comparison by the scalar-adjunction mate of the exact restriction/pullback square [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], conjugated by the canonical intrinsic-realization comparison. The comparison on $Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ is the unique isomorphism that, in every pair of primitive-root charts related by $\zeta_m=\zeta_n^{\ell^{n-m}}$, becomes this pullback comparison and the canonical shift comparison. For separated finite-type schemes, define the compact-support comparison [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] as the scalar adjunct of compact support of the scalar unit followed by the canonical proper/open restriction comparison. The exceptional comparison [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is the unique arrow whose compact-support transpose is the reduced counit of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Use the exceptional realization coordinates of [thm-pur-composition-coherence]. The coefficient-unit comparison is the scalar adjunct of the degree-zero coefficient map, fixed on all ring sections. These are the six-operation finite-reduction maps, rather than arbitrary endpoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Operation, root-line, twist and shift comparisons; finite-reduction proof

proof.text: For the pullback presentation use the specified native isomorphism; heterogeneous equality fixes it uniquely. The coefficient square is the existing naturality identity of constant inverse image, specialized to the lifted quotient ring map.
The coefficient-ring map gives a sectionwise additive, restriction-linear natural module map. Equality on every section proves uniqueness of the ordinary unit map.

Apply finiteCompactSupportScalarComparison to the actual quotient, chosen compactification and original input. The finite-Tor predicate supplies bounded constructibility, and finiteReduction_preserves_ctf supplies bounded constructibility of its actual reduction. The defining scalar-adjunction formula is the comparison in this node.

Transport the published bounded-etale-origin counit Hom bijection through the intrinsic realization equivalences and the canonical support realization comparison. compositionInput_bounded supplies its boundedness hypotheses. Smooth exceptional preservation and finite reduction preservation put the required source and target in that domain. Apply surjectivity to inverse of the support comparison followed by the reduced counit. Injectivity and cancellation of that support isomorphism prove uniqueness.

The coefficient prime is nonzero in the algebraically closed base, so choose a primitive ell^n-th root using HasEnoughRootsOfUnity.exists_primitiveRoot. IsPrimitiveRoot.pow gives the compatible primitive ell^m-th root, using n=(n-m)+m. Compose scalar extension of the original root chart, the canonical shift and pullback comparisons, and the inverse reduced root chart. Root-chart independence gives the normalization for every compatible pair; cancellation of any one reduced chart proves uniqueness.

The degree-zero free rank-one ring module is K-flat: tensoring any acyclic complex with it is the complex itself by the right unitor. The normalized universal derived scalar counit therefore computes its scalar extension. The ordinary scalar unit is multiplication, by scalarExtensionUnitIso and its pure-section formula. The normalized ordinary adjunction sends this isomorphism to the prescribed ring-section map. On complexes concentrated in degree zero, the defining derived-unit equation and the exact restriction single-object comparison identify its derived adjunct with the universal counit followed by localization of the ordinary multiplication isomorphism. This is invertible, and the coefficient realization models transport it to finiteReductionUnitComparison.

Write the two positive exponents as n+1 and m+1. Use the full inclusion of the specified invertible finite exceptional mate to form finiteReductionExceptionalFiniteModel. Its purity counit identity is lem-pur-finite-reduction-exceptional-model-counit. Uniqueness in existsUnique_finiteReductionExceptionalComparison identifies this isomorphism hom with the chosen exceptional comparison; rewrite by that equality and use the isomorphism instance.

proof_origin.place: Earlier six proved obligations retained; the exceptional comparison is reduced to normalization of the existing finite exceptional isomorphism by its counit and uniqueness.
